newsitem.title: USA: Calif. tax board denies Pacific Bell tax break.
newsitem.headline: Calif. tax board denies Pacific Bell tax break.

text.p: The California state Board of Equalization said on Wednesday that it rejected a request by Pacific Telesis Group's Pacific Bell unit to cut its property taxes by $48 million.
The board voted 3-to-2 against Pacific Bell's request to have its assessed value decreased by $4.3 billion, which would have saved it $48 million in property taxes per year.

"The BOE correctly and appropriately denied Pacific Bell's request today," said Johan Klehs, who chairs the Board of Equalization. "The $48 million in tax revenue is earmarked for counties, cities, and special districts."
Pacific Bell lost its first hearing on this issue in May, the Board of Equalization said.

At issue Wednesday was Pacific Bell's accounting method. The Board of Equalization said Pacific Bell, despite signing an agreement in 1992 that set forth the accounting method to be used, attempted to change its procedures.

"Pacific Bell's attempt to change the rules disregards the fact that no single event or events occurred in 1995 that altered Pacific Bell's ability to operate or the general value of its assets," Klehs said. "Their petition did not pass the 'reasonableness test.'"
The Board of Equalization has the responsibility to assess values on the property of utilities throughout the state. It also hears tax case appeals on business, property and income tax cases.
